shared_text:
The flight. A regional jet on a passenger flight, flying an ILS approach by day.

The crew. The captain was the pilot monitoring and was also acting as an instructor. The other pilot was the pilot flying.

What happened. Inbound on the ILS approach, ATC instructed the crew to maintain 5,000 ft to a fix on the approach and cleared them for the approach. The vertical navigation path was set at 2.0 degrees, so it showed the path below their altitude of 5,000 ft. Before the fix, flight path angle mode was selected to 'chase' the path. The captain stated that they were supposed to maintain altitude until the fix. The aircraft started to descend below the assigned 5,000 ft. ATC queried their altitude, instructed them to climb back to 5,000 ft and maintain it until the fix, and cleared them again for the approach. The crew climbed back to 5,000 ft.
safe_outcome: The aircraft maintained 5,000 ft until the fix, and the approach was flown with no further issues. There was no conflict with other traffic. No one was hurt and the aircraft was not damaged.
bad_outcome: Another aircraft was climbing nearby. Both crews received TCAS resolution advisories and followed them, and the aircraft passed about 300 feet vertically and half a mile apart. A flight attendant on this aircraft was thrown against a galley cart during the manoeuvre and received a minor injury.
bracket_fill: [climbing / descending / crossing] = climbing; [this aircraft] = this aircraft
notes: Nothing to remove under rule 3: the report has no Cause or Suggestions section. The report is short (one narrative of seven sentences), so the shared text is under 150 words; deviation D5 applies and nothing was added. The report does not say who selected flight path angle mode, so the passive is kept; the pilot flying is called 'the other pilot' because the report gives no other role for them. Kept as said at the time: the captain's statement that they were to maintain altitude until the fix. 'By day' is from the coded local time, 1201-1800. Moved under rule 5: maintaining 5,000 ft to the fix and flying the approach with no further issues. Removed under rule 6: the fix name, the runway and the airport. Judgement call: 'climbing', for traffic below the assigned altitude such as a departure.
